items.question: What is the recommended R22 takeoff and climb airspeed?
items.explanation: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS: takeoff and climb 60 KIAS; maximum rate of climb (VY) 53 KIAS; maximum range 83 KIAS; landing approach 60 KIAS; autorotation 60–70 KIAS.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the R22 speed for maximum rate of climb (VY)?
items.explanation: Maximum rate of climb (VY) is 53 KIAS.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the recommended R22 maximum-range airspeed?
items.explanation: Maximum range airspeed is 83 KIAS (certain conditions may require lower — see the Vne placards).
references: R22 POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: During the daily/preflight main-rotor check, how should a blade be lowered for inspection?
options: Pull down on the blade you want to lower
Push up on the opposite blade
Apply the rotor brake and rotate
items.explanation: A caution states: do not pull down on blades to teeter the rotor. To lower a blade, push up on the opposite blade.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS – Main Rotor (p.4-4)

items.question: What is the maximum acceptable V-belt slack found during the engine right-side preflight check?
items.explanation: During the engine right-side check, V-belt slack must be 1.5 inches (4 cm) maximum.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS – Engine Right Side (p.4-2)

items.question: What is the engine oil quantity range checked during the left-side preflight?
items.explanation: Engine oil is checked at 4–6 qt during the engine left-side preflight; the minimum for takeoff is 4 qt.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS – Engine Left Side (p.4-3)

items.question: In the BEFORE STARTING ENGINE checklist, what position is the governor switch set to?
items.explanation: The Before Starting Engine list ends with Governor switch — ON (altimeter set, clutch disengaged, carb heat OFF, mixture full rich, primer down and locked).
references: R22 POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: In the BEFORE STARTING ENGINE checks, how are the collective and cyclic set?
options: Collective full up, cyclic aft, friction OFF
Collective full down with friction ON, cyclic neutral with friction ON
items.explanation: Before Starting Engine: collective full down with friction ON; cyclic neutral with friction ON; pedals neutral; rotor brake disengaged.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: After the starter engages, blades should begin turning within how many seconds?
items.explanation: During start, with the clutch switch engaged, blades should be turning in less than 5 seconds; excessive belt slack may let belts jump the sheave grooves.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7); Sec 7 CLUTCH ACTUATOR (p.7-9)

items.question: Within how long after starting should oil pressure reach at least 25 psi?
items.explanation: During start: oil pressure 25 psi minimum within 30 seconds.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: What is the maximum magneto drop at 75% RPM during run-up, and over what time?
items.explanation: Mag drop at 75% RPM: 7% maximum, within 2 seconds.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: During run-up with the governor on, to what RPM is the throttle increased?
items.explanation: Governor ON, increase throttle — RPM 102–104%. Then verify warning lights out, and check the horn/light at 97% by lifting the collective slightly and reducing RPM.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: Why should continuous operation at 60–70% rotor speed be avoided during start and run-up?
items.explanation: A caution during starting and run-up directs avoiding continuous operation at 60–70% rotor speed to minimise tail resonance.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: Before takeoff, at what RPM should the rotor be stabilised?
items.explanation: Takeoff procedure step 1: verify doors latched, governor ON, and RPM stabilised at 102–104%. If RPM drops below 102% during the climb, lower collective.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: TAKEOFF PROCEDURE (p.4-8)

items.question: How should a normal R22 takeoff to the hover be made?
options: Snatch the collective up to break ground quickly
Slowly raise collective until light on the skids, reposition cyclic for equilibrium, then gently lift into a hover
Roll forward on the skids and pull pitch
Apply full aft cyclic then collective
items.explanation: Slowly raise collective until the aircraft is light on the skids, reposition cyclic as required for equilibrium, then gently lift into a hover; check gages in the green and adjust carb heat if required.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: TAKEOFF PROCEDURE (p.4-8)

items.question: Why must the pilot never inadvertently pull the mixture control in flight?
options: It sets off the CO detector
items.explanation: A cruise caution warns to exercise extreme care never to inadvertently pull the mixture control, as engine stoppage will result. Always reach around the left side of the cyclic post to actuate the lateral trim.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: CRUISE (p.4-8); Sec 7 CONTROL TRIM AND FRICTION (p.7-7)

items.question: Why is in-flight leaning with the mixture control not recommended in the R22?
options: It raises the CHT above limits
There is no propeller to keep the engine turning if overleaning occurs, so engine stoppage may result
items.explanation: A cruise caution notes in-flight leaning is not recommended because there is no propeller to keep the engine turning should overleaning occur — engine stoppage may result.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: CRUISE (p.4-8)

items.question: During doors-off operation, which door does the POH prefer to leave installed, and why?
options: The right door, for pilot protection
The left door, to protect the tail rotor from loose objects
Both must always be removed together
items.explanation: Avoid removing the left door to protect the tail rotor from loose objects. If it must be removed, warn the passenger to secure loose objects and keep head and arms inside the cabin.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DOORS-OFF OPERATION (p.4-9)

items.question: Why must a simulated engine failure never be initiated by chopping the throttle?
options: To avoid inadvertent engine stoppage — always roll the throttle off smoothly
items.explanation: A practice-autorotation caution: to avoid inadvertent engine stoppage, do not chop the throttle to simulate a power failure — always roll it off smoothly, and recover immediately if the engine is rough or engine RPM continues to drop.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-9)

items.question: Below what engine RPM is the governor inactive, regardless of switch position?
items.explanation: A note in the practice-autorotation procedure states the governor is inactive below 80% engine RPM regardless of the governor switch position.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-9)

items.question: When entering autorotation from above 4000 feet, what should be done to prevent engine overspeed?
options: Reduce throttle slightly before lowering collective
items.explanation: A note directs reducing throttle slightly before lowering collective when entering autorotation from above 4000 feet, to prevent engine overspeed.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-9)

items.question: Catastrophic rotor stall could occur if rotor RPM ever drops below what value?
items.explanation: A caution warns that catastrophic rotor stall could occur if rotor RPM ever drops below 80% plus 1% per 1000 ft of altitude — simulated engine failures require prompt lowering of the collective.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-9)

items.question: For a practice autorotation with ground contact, what is done differently before the cyclic flare?
options: Raise collective to arrest the descent
Roll the throttle off into the overtravel spring and hold it against the hard stop until the autorotation is complete
items.explanation: Prior to the cyclic flare, roll the throttle off into the overtravel spring and hold it against the hard stop until the autorotation is complete — this prevents the throttle correlator from adding power when collective is raised. Always contact the ground skids level, nose straight ahead.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION - WITH GROUND CONTACT (p.4-10)

items.question: In what OAT range is carburetor ice most likely to form?
options: Between -4°C and 30°C with an OAT–dew point spread under 15 C°
items.explanation: Carburetor ice is most likely when OAT is between -4°C and 30°C (25°F and 86°F) and the difference between OAT and dew point is less than 15 C°.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: USE OF CARBURETOR HEAT (p.4-11)

items.question: During descent and autorotation at power settings below 18 inches MAP, how should carburetor heat be used?
options: Only if the CAT gage enters the yellow arc
Apply full carburetor heat regardless of the CAT gage indication
Leave carb heat off to preserve power
items.explanation: Below 18 inches MAP, apply full carb heat regardless of the CAT gage — the gage does not indicate correct carburetor temperature below 18 inches MAP.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: USE OF CARBURETOR HEAT (p.4-11)

items.question: Why must the pilot actively manage carb heat even though the governor is holding RPM and MAP steady?
options: The governor increases carb heat automatically only on the O-360
The pilot may be unaware of carburetor ice forming because the governor automatically increases throttle to hold MAP and RPM constant
Carb ice trips the governor-off light
It is required by AD to cycle carb heat every 5 minutes
items.explanation: A caution notes the pilot may be unaware of carburetor ice formation because the governor automatically increases throttle to maintain constant manifold pressure and RPM — so carb heat must be applied whenever icing conditions are suspected.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: USE OF CARBURETOR HEAT (p.4-11); Safety Notice SN-31

items.question: How should a descent be initiated in the R22?
items.explanation: A caution states: do not initiate a descent with forward cyclic — this can produce a low-G condition. Always initiate a descent by lowering collective.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING (p.4-12)

items.question: On the approach, the rate of descent should be less than what value before airspeed is reduced below 30 KIAS?
items.explanation: Reduce airspeed and altitude smoothly to a hover — be sure the rate of descent is less than 300 FPM before airspeed is reduced below 30 KIAS (vortex ring state avoidance).
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING (p.4-12)

items.question: In the shutdown procedure, how long must the pilot wait after moving the clutch switch to disengage before pulling the mixture off?
items.explanation: Shutdown: collective down at 70–75% RPM friction on, throttle closed after the CHT drop, clutch switch disengage, wait 30 seconds then mixture OFF, mixture guard back on, wait 30 seconds then apply rotor brake.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE (p.4-13)

items.question: If ambient temperature is above 100°F (38°C), what does the shutdown note require before reducing to idle?
options: Cool down at 70–75% RPM for at least one minute
Cool down at idle for five minutes
items.explanation: A shutdown note: if ambient temperature is above 100°F (38°C), cool down at 70–75% RPM for at least one minute before reducing to idle.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE (p.4-13)

items.question: Why must collective pitch not be used to slow the rotor during shutdown?
options: The blades may flap and strike the tailcone
items.explanation: A caution: do not slow the rotor by raising collective during shutdown — the blades may flap and strike the tailcone (collective pitch can disengage the droop-stop friction).
references: R22 POH Sec 4: SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE (p.4-13); Sec 10 Safety Tip 14

items.question: Per AD 95-26-04 information in Section 4, what cruise airspeed band should R22 pilots maintain?
options: Between 60 KIAS and less than 0.9 Vne, but no lower than 57 KIAS
As fast as possible up to Vne
items.explanation: The Section 4 AD 95-26-04 recommendations: maintain cruise airspeeds between 60 KIAS and less than 0.9 Vne but no lower than 57 KIAS; use maximum power-on RPM at all times; avoid sideslip; avoid large rapid forward cyclic inputs.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: INFORMATION PER FAA AD 95-26-04 (p.4-15)

items.question: During the daily/preflight cowl-doors check, what is done with the warning light test switches?
options: Pushed to test (with battery switch ON)
Checked for continuity with a meter
items.explanation: Cowl doors check (battery switch ON): oil pressure and alternator lights ON, warning light test switches — push to test, check EMU status if installed, check fuel quantity, then battery switch OFF.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS – Cowl Doors (p.4-1)

items.question: What confirms correct sprag clutch operation during run-up?
items.explanation: During run-up the sprag clutch check is confirmed by the tachometer needles splitting.
references: R22 POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)
